about: Judge calibration registry (RIMMANDRAKE_SEED_JUDGE_CALIBRATION_FROM_CORPORA; spec design/specs/2026-11-12-refusal-contract-for-judges-and-gates.md section 5). Keyed by family; `hash` is refusal_contract.brief_hash of `brief`. Only a CALIBRATED brief's verdict, either way, has a consequence (a refusal sends work back, a pass signs); any edit to a brief file resets it to UNTESTED (refusal_contract.py calibrate). A brief is CALIBRATED only by a check on its current hash whose case results show every `planted` case ran and came out as planted, good and bad both (refusal_contract.judge_cases; RIMMANDRAKE_EARN_CALIBRATION_BOTH_WAYS): `free_check` is deterministic and runs on every calibrate, `model_check` spends and runs only on `calibrate --model <family>`. `cases` is prose about the corpora a row was seeded from.

proposals: Plants: say whether D3's footprint test is judged on the full drawSize canvas or after visualSizeRange.max scaling (here 0.7). subject.json gives both, and this brief does not say which one D3 means. Today the sprite passes either way, but a plant drawn to the full canvas with a small visualMax could be judged differently by different judges.

Plants with one-sided art (like this fern, which sweeps to one side by design): consider a line on whether the game's random mesh flip may mirror a directional feature the description depends on ('swept to the cold side'). This is a game-behaviour question that a still picture cannot settle, so it is a proposal only.

verdicts.notes: Candidate B; no keep on record, so E3 does not apply. The plant is a painterly deep-green fern clump with no drawn keyline (B1, B1a). The edge pixels are only slightly darker than the interior (mean luminance 61 at the edge against 72 inside, measured), which is shading, not an outline. Every frond sweeps to one side, as if combed, and the pale rachis shows on each frond, so the picture matches its description. Alpha is real: on a magenta backdrop it has no halo, backdrop, ground shadow or stone prop. The only faint pixels are a few alpha-1 specks out to the canvas edge, which are invisible. At alpha 16 or more the plant sits inside x 16–240 and y 22–236 of the 256 px canvas (D4, D3). The canvas is 256 px for drawSize 1, which is generous (D2). In scale.png the fern sits within one cell beside the human at 256 px/cell, and in playzoom_single.png it reads at 32 px/cell as a few bold dark-green frond shapes, clearly apart from the tan ground. That is not grey mud (B2). Plants have one picture and no facings, so the C lines do not apply. There is no canon entry, donor, sibling keep or owner note in subject.json, and the subject is not a pawn.

A line that turns an invented subject's description into yes/no checks would let a judge refuse this.

proposals: Facing anatomy agreement: add to C2 an explicit clause that a large appendage (fan, sail, frill, wing) keeps one attachment point and one plane across facings, and is drawn foreshortened accordingly. Opacity: body pixels on all three facings sit at alpha ~253 rather than 255 (median 253, measured). That makes the creature very slightly see-through over ground textures. Propose that D4's 'real alpha' state that interior body pixels are fully opaque. Advisory, not refused here.

Description states: the subject description says 'folded flat or blazing open — closed it is a blade, open it is a wheel'. No constraint says which state the base sprite must show, or that a pawn with only one graphic must pick one. All three facings show it open, which is consistent. Propose a line stating that a creature with a described display state draws its resting state in the base graphic unless the owner says otherwise.

proposals: C1 says that north shows 'no face, no eyes', but this subject's description ('extra eyes opened in its hide') requires eyes on the hide all over the body, including along the spine and tail that north.png shows. B2 is judged against the one tan soil in scale.png. A creature whose palette matches that soil fails while it might pass on darker or greener ground, and the reverse can also happen. Proposal: the scale panel shows the 32 px/cell copy on two contrasting grounds (one light tan, one dark or green), so that 'blends into the ground' is judged on more than one ground.

C2 gives no method for measuring size across facings. Proposal: compare a rigid span the facings share (shoulder or crown to the foot baseline, or leg thickness) between the facings, rather than the canvas fill. Side views of long animals fill the canvas width, so a fill-the-canvas habit makes the south and north facings systematically oversized, as happened here (about 1.35x).
